news.headline: Afghanistan faces deepening humanitarian crisis amid sweeping rights restrictions
news.summary: Afghanistan stands at a “difficult crossroad” more than five years after the Taliban returned to power, a senior UN official said on Friday. Relative stability and security are being undercut by a fragile economy, sweeping curbs on rights and acute humanitarian need.

news.headline: World News in Brief: Civilians killed in DR Congo, Ukrainians wrestle with return, Guterres calls out ‘normalisation’ of force
news.summary: At least 30 civilians were killed overnight on Thursday in Beni Territory, North Kivu in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, according to local sources&nbsp;cited by the UN aid coordination office (OCHA).

news.headline: Sudan’s suffering is plain for all to see say aid teams, as brutal war continues
news.summary: Aid teams working to help millions of people uprooted by the ongoing war in Sudan appealed on Friday for more international assistance amid desperate funding shortages, empty warehouses and overwhelming needs.&nbsp;

news.headline: World News in Brief: Korea tensions mount, UN demands answers over staff death in Yemen, Guterres in Spain, Nepal alert ahead of COP31
news.summary: UN Secretary-General António Guterres remains concerned over the situation on the Korean Peninsula, including the potential escalation of tensions across the Demilitarized Zone (DMZ), his Spokesperson said on Thursday.

news.headline: Abyei: Deadly drone strikes mark ‘new and concerning’ threat, UN peacekeeping chief warns
news.summary: Drone strikes that killed at least 30 people in Abyei last month have added “a new and concerning dimension” to security in the disputed area, the UN’s peacekeeping chief told the Security Council on Thursday.

news.headline: Children at risk as war zone attacks on water and sanitation more than triple
news.summary: Attacks that damaged or destroyed water and sanitation systems in conflict zones tripled between 2021 and 2025, increasing children’s risk of exposure to disease outbreaks, malnutrition and violence.

news.headline: Two new Ebola vaccines to join DR Congo clinical trial
news.summary: Two new Ebola vaccine candidates will be added to a clinical trial in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) as the country continues to battle a deadly outbreak caused by the Bundibugyo species of the virus.&nbsp;&nbsp;

news.headline: UN peacekeeping chief warns of ‘security vacuum’ as Blue Helmets leave Lebanon and Western Sahara
news.summary: The UN’s peacekeeping chief warned on Wednesday that the withdrawal of “Blue Helmets” from Lebanon and Western Sahara risks leaving a dangerous security vacuum, while the Security Council remains divided over what, if anything, should replace them.

news.headline: Gunfire damages tents at Rafah displacement site in Gaza, as aid teams prepare for winter storms
news.summary: Gunfire hit and damaged multiple tents at a displacement site in Gaza’s northern Rafah region on Tuesday, reportedly causing injuries and forcing a humanitarian partner to leave the area, the UN aid coordination office (OCHA) has&nbsp;said.

news.headline: Fuel price shock: Why developing economies are paying the most at the pump
news.summary: When war shut the Strait of Hormuz in February, oil prices soared everywhere. But the pain at the pump has been far from equal, and the world’s developing economies are paying the heaviest price, according to a&nbsp;new report from UNCTAD, the UN trade and development agency.

news.headline: Syria’s undocumented children ‘pay the price’ of war and a law that shuts out mothers
news.summary: Many children born in Syria since the war began in 2011 have no legal identity because nationality passes only through fathers – many of whom are dead or missing – a member of the independent UN commission investigating rights violations in the country said on Wednesday.

news.headline: Afghan children face narrowing path to education, UN agencies report
news.summary: More than half of Afghanistan’s children who should be in primary school remain outside formal learning and millions of girls can only dream of going to university.

news.headline: ‘This is not about politics. This is about people’: UN warns of impact of deadly drone strikes in Sudan
news.summary: Intensifying drone attacks on civilian infrastructure across Sudan are disrupting electricity, water and fuel supplies, putting lives at risk and hampering the delivery of humanitarian aid, the UN’s top official in the country has warned.&nbsp;

news.headline: World News in Brief: Children killed in Myanmar strike, new violence flares in Mozambique, an Internet affordability milestone
news.summary: A school in Myanmar has been hit in an airstrike, with&nbsp;three children reported killed and five others injured, according to UN Children’s Fund&nbsp;UNICEF.

news.headline: Married off at 14: In Yemen’s war, women and girls suffer ‘devastating consequences’
news.summary: Safa is 14. Her mother died earlier this year. She has no brothers or sisters. And a few weeks ago, as the crisis took hold, her father married her to an elderly man, afraid that if he were killed in the hostilities, no one would be left to protect her.

news.headline: Air raid alerts and attacks on schools: the devastating face of education in Ukraine
news.summary: Ukraine has sustained almost 2,000 attacks on education since the full-scale Russian invasion in 2022, with some 270 this year alone, the UN Children’s Fund (UNICEF) said on Tuesday, a day after a strike at a school being used to distribute aid.

news.headline: World News in Brief: healthcare crisis in Yemen’s Taiz and Afghanistan, Western Sahara mission's phased closure
news.summary: The humanitarian crisis in Yemen is worsening, particularly in the southwestern city of Taiz, which is being encircled by paramilitary Iran-backed Houthi forces.&nbsp;

news.headline: Ukraine: WFP provides hot meals to Oleshky evacuees as UN pushes to restore power before winter
news.summary: The UN World Food Programme (WFP) is providing emergency food assistance to more than 400 people who were able to leave the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky, in Ukraine’s Kherson region, during a brief local ceasefire.&nbsp;

news.headline: Ethiopia: Violence in the north is pushing health system to the brink, WHO chief warns
news.summary: The head of the World Health Organization (WHO) called on Monday for greater protection for civilians caught in conflict in northern Ethiopia following deadly drone strikes this past weekend.

news.headline: Western Sahara: UN ‘stands ready’ to keep supporting peace efforts as MINURSO mission ends
news.summary: The UN remains committed to supporting a just, lasting and mutually acceptable political solution in Western Sahara that provides for the self-determination of its people, Secretary-General António Guterres said on Sunday, as the UN peacekeeping mission there began to wind down.

news.headline: ‘They deserve to know the truth’: UN rights chief demands probe into staffer’s death in Houthi custody
news.summary: The UN human rights chief on Saturday demanded an independent investigation into the death of a Yemeni colleague held by the Houthis for more than two years, whose family learned of his death only weeks after it happened.

news.headline: Somalia looks to the future as the UN's political mission closes
news.summary: “The story of the UN's political engagement in Somalia has been one of persistence, partnership and adaptation,”&nbsp;Raisedon Zenenga, the UN Secretary-General's Deputy Special Representative for Somalia has said, as three decades of UN political missions in the Horn of Africa country

news.headline: Samarkand: A ‘living museum’ on the Silk Road grapples with a tourism boom
news.summary: As the sun sets over Samarkand’s majestic Registan, its last rays glint across the turquoise mosaics. Dusk settles on the ancient square where great trade routes have crossed for centuries.

news.headline: DPR Korea: Isolation deepens even as the country changes, says UN rights official
news.summary: The Democratic People’s Republic of Korea (DPRK) is building factories and hospitals, rolling out smartphones and mobile banking, and passing new laws at an unprecedented rate. But its people are more cut off from the outside world than at any point in the country’s history.

news.headline: World News in Brief: 300,000 displaced in Lebanon, Türk ‘deeply concerned’ over Novaya Gazeta closure, $50 million refugee appeal, World Cities Day
news.summary: More than 300,000 people displaced since early March remain internally displaced in Lebanon, where the humanitarian crisis is&nbsp;“far from over,” according to the UN’s aid coordination office (OCHA).

news.headline: UN rights office warns of deepening displacement ‘nightmare’ in Gaza
news.summary: Israeli forces continue to push Palestinians into ever-smaller areas of the Gaza Strip while destroying civilian infrastructure and attacking displacement sites, the UN human rights office, OHCHR, warned on Friday amid concerns of ethnic cleansing.&nbsp;

news.headline: Yemen war makes reaching assistance too dangerous for many
news.summary: More than 280,000 people have now been displaced by fighting in Yemen and many vulnerable people are unable to access lifesaving relief because it is too dangerous to do so, the UN refugee agency (UNHCR) said on Friday.

news.headline: DR Congo: Hunger deepens for millions amid conflict, Ebola and climate shocks
news.summary: More than 28 million people in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) are not getting enough to eat and the number is expected to tick up in the coming months, according to the latest alert from the IPC global food security monitor.&nbsp;

news.headline: Ukraine: Oleshky ceasefire offers ‘hope’ for civilians as attacks on aid vehicles continue
news.summary: Each day the ceasefire in Oleshky holds means hope for civilians in the city, the UN’s top humanitarian official said, stressing that those wishing to leave must be able to do so safely and voluntarily.

news.headline: Myanmar’s illicit economy fuels escalating violence, with civilians bearing the brunt
news.summary: Myanmar’s human rights situation is “catastrophic”, the&nbsp;UN independent expert on the country warned at a press briefing Thursday, as the war spirals with no end in sight.&nbsp;

news.headline: Afghanistan opium production jumps fivefold as farmers find ways round Taliban ban
news.summary: Opium production in Afghanistan has risen fivefold in a year. According to a UN survey released on Thursday, it’s the first significant increase since the Taliban banned poppy cultivation in 2022.

news.headline: Civilians in Sudan’s El Obeid trapped between drones and incarceration
news.summary: Civilians in Sudan’s El Obeid live in constant fear of drone attacks by the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) and of a wave of arbitrary arrests by the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF), UN-appointed independent investigators said on Wednesday.&nbsp;

news.headline: DR Congo: WHO urges sustained efforts as Ebola cases top 10,000
news.summary: As Ebola cases in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) surpass the 10,000 mark, the World Health Organization (WHO) has underlined the need for continued efforts to contain spread of the disease.&nbsp;

news.headline: Higher Ground: How New York is raising a park to hold back the sea
news.summary: On 29 October 2012, Hurricane Sandy slammed into New York City, unleashing a devastating storm surge that flooded homes, subways and tunnels, knocked out power and sparked deadly fires.&nbsp;

news.headline: Backing for UN call to end Cuba embargo falls to 20-year low
news.summary: The UN General Assembly on Wednesday called for the 34th time for an end to the US economic, commercial and financial embargo on Cuba – but with the weakest backing for the resolution in two decades.

news.headline: Gaza: Families brace for fourth winter in tents as aid operations remain stymied
news.summary: Families in Gaza are bracing for a fourth winter in tents and makeshift shelters as UN aid operations face mounting obstacles, with transport suspended on Tuesday due to Israel’s closure of the key Kerem Shalom crossing for election day.&nbsp;

news.headline: Ebola: 20 contacts released from quarantine in Kenya, amid vaccine ‘hope’ in DR Congo
news.summary: Twenty people associated with Kenya’s first case of Ebola Bundibugyo virus disease have been reunited with their families after being released from quarantine following completion of a mandatory 21-day monitoring period.&nbsp;
